kicker: Six stones make a path; the clearer the request, the brighter the lantern.

path.label: Stone path to the lantern
path.group: The six stones of a prompt. Drag, or tap each one, to place it on the path.
path.place: Place the “{name}” stone on the path
path.again: {name}: already on the path, tap to read again
path.art: A stone lantern on raked sand. Each stone placed on the path makes it glow brighter.

blocks.name: Role
blocks.title: Role
blocks.example: “You are a copywriter for a Vietnamese lipstick brand.”

blocks.name: Context
blocks.title: Context
blocks.example: “Readers: busy women aged 20–30. Goal: launch a new lipstick.”

blocks.name: Data / examples
blocks.title: Data / examples
blocks.hint: raw facts and a sample line
blocks.example: “Brick Red matte lipstick, soft on the lips. Sample voice: ‘Warm lips for chilly days.’”

blocks.name: Constraints
blocks.title: Constraints
blocks.example: “Each line under 20 words, warm tone, never use the word ‘best’.”

path.insight: A clear prompt (your request to AI) has six parts: role, context, task, data, constraints, format.
path.detail: You don’t always need all six. But the more important the task, the more context and examples help.

compare.label: Two requests
compare.send: Send both requests to the same AI

weakReply.t: . Buy now before it sells out!

strongReply: Brick Red: matte yet soft — warm lips all through a busy day. #BrickRed
Chilly afternoon? One swipe of Brick Red is warmth enough. #MatteBrickRed
compare.done: The AI has answered both requests.
compare.insight: Same AI: a sloppy request gets a vague answer, a clear one gets exactly what you need.

detail.text: Both answers are pre-written examples; a real AI may answer a little differently each time.

rules.label: Six golden rules
rules.group: Six golden rules, one stone each

items.title: Be as clear as briefing a new hire
items.example: AI doesn’t know your company, customers or taste — tell it everything.

items.title: Give examples
items.example: Paste a sample you like; AI will pick up its voice.

items.title: Break big jobs into small steps
items.example: Outline first, write next, edit last — one step per turn.

items.title: Ask back, go a few rounds
items.example: Ask: “What else do you need to know?”, then refine over a few turns.

items.title: Ask AI to check itself
items.example: “Review this for me: what might be wrong or made up?”

items.title: Don’t share sensitive data
items.example: Passwords, card numbers, customer records: keep them out, or hide names before pasting.

rules.insight: Few people write a great prompt on the first try: be clear, give samples, split steps, refine, keep private data private.
rules.detail: Small tip: end your prompt with “Before answering, review your work and ask me if anything is missing.”

quiz.q: To get the caption you want from AI, what should you do?
options: Give a role, context, examples, constraints
Paste the whole customer phone list
Write as much as possible, longer is better
quiz.explain: A complete request tells AI who reads it, what’s needed and what to avoid; sensitive data stays with you.

summary: Ask AI like you’d brief a new hire: be clear, give examples, set limits.
